subject: english-studies
title: Full stop, question mark and comma
summary: Use the three most common punctuation marks so your writing is easy to read.

lesson.text: Punctuation marks are signs that help the reader. They show where a sentence ends, when a question is asked, and where to pause.
A full stop ends a sentence that tells us something.
A question mark ends a sentence that asks something. Questions often start with who, what, where, when, why, how, is, are, can or do.
A comma shows a short pause. Use it to separate things in a list, and after yes or no at the start of an answer.

items: I bought rice, beans, oil and pepper.
Yes, I have finished my homework.

lesson.text: In a list, there is usually no comma before the last "and" in Nigerian school English.

lesson.title: Punctuate: did you see uche ada and kemi
steps: It asks something, so it ends with a question mark.
Uche, Ada and Kemi are a list of names, so put a comma after Uche.
Add capitals to the first word and the names.
Did you see Uche, Ada and Kemi?

lesson.text: Read your sentence aloud. Where your voice stops, you need a full stop. Where it rises to ask, you need a question mark.

questions.prompt: Which mark should end this sentence: What time is it
questions.explanation: "What time is it" asks something, so it ends with a question mark.

options: I like mangoes, oranges and pawpaw.
I like, mangoes oranges and pawpaw.
I like mangoes oranges, and pawpaw?
I like mangoes oranges and pawpaw
questions.explanation: The comma separates the fruits in the list, and the sentence tells us something, so it ends with a full stop.

questions.prompt: Which sentence needs a full stop, not a question mark?
questions.explanation: "My brother is a nurse" tells us something, so it ends with a full stop. The others ask questions.

questions.prompt: Where does the comma go? "No I have not seen it."
questions.explanation: Put a comma after yes or no at the start of an answer: "No, I have not seen it."
